target.title: chore(cli): cover HF local app flow
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hugging Face local-app snippets can point OpenClaw at local OpenAI-compatible servers such as llama.cpp and MLX LM.
Before this change, OpenClaw did not have a focused CLI regression test proving that the documented custom-provider flow still configures those snippets and can run `agent --local` against them.
This matters because a config schema change, onboarding flag change, or streaming request change could break those snippets without a model download ever being involved.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a deterministic CLI contract test that exercises the real `onboard` command and the real `agent --local` command.
The test uses a fake OpenAI-compatible local server, so it validates OpenClaw behavior without downloading or running HF models.

- Covers the `llama-cpp` provider with `ggml-org/gemma-4-E4B-it-GGUF:Q4_K_M`.
- Covers the `mlx-lm` provider with `mlx-community/Qwen3-0.6B-4bit`.
- Verifies that onboarding writes the expected provider config, base URL, model list, and primary model.
- Verifies that the local agent sends a streaming chat completion request to the configured local endpoint.

## User Impact

Users should not see behavior changes from this PR.
Maintainers get regression coverage for the Hugging Face local-app OpenClaw snippet path, including the CLI flags users are expected to run.

## Related PR

- Hugging Face JS local-app snippet change: https://github.com/huggingface/huggingface.js/pull/2185

## Evidence

I ran the focused regression test and the relevant local checks.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts test/huggingface-local-app-openclaw.e2e.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/huggingface-local-app-openclaw.e2e.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src`
- `git diff --check`
